cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

mechanism: A treats B repair as a pupil attempt needing correction and negotiates public credit to gain actual control of the tool.
confusable: Not merely teaching technique: A seeks the screwdriver and hands-on control of the mishandled repair.
comparison: Tool custody with credit protection versus control of a socially risky seating plan.
seedUse: D36 repair/credit bargaining already works with S05 grading a pupil attempt; preserve the original for rereading rather than automatically replacing it.
